सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 कैसे भरें? (How to Apply Online)

हर साल लाखों उम्मीदवार सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 भरने की प्रक्रिया में गलतियाँ कर बैठते हैं, जिससे उनका आवेदन रद्द हो सकता है। नीचे दी गई सरल प्रक्रिया से आप अपना फॉर्म सही तरीके से भर सकते हैं।

आवेदन की चरणबद्ध प्रक्रिया

  1. संबंधित विभाग की आधिकारिक अधिसूचना (Notification PDF) ध्यान से पढ़ें और अपनी पात्रता जांचें।
  2. वैध ईमेल आईडी और मोबाइल नंबर से पोर्टल पर पंजीकरण (Registration) करें।
  3. व्यक्तिगत विवरण, शैक्षणिक योग्यता, और आवश्यक दस्तावेज़ अपलोड करें (फोटो, हस्ताक्षर, प्रमाणपत्र)।
  4. निर्धारित आवेदन शुल्क का ऑनलाइन भुगतान करें और भुगतान की रसीद सुरक्षित रखें।
  5. फॉर्म सबमिट करने से पहले सभी जानकारी की दोबारा जांच करें और फॉर्म का प्रिंटआउट अवश्य लें।

Documents Required for Sarkari Form

Typical documents needed: recent passport-size photograph (as per specified size/format), scanned signature, educational certificates and mark sheets, category certificate (if applicable), and a valid ID proof (Aadhaar/PAN).

Common Mistakes to Avoid While Applying

  • Submitting a photo or signature that doesn't match the specified pixel/size requirements.
  • Missing the last date due to server load - apply at least 2–3 days before deadline.
  • Entering a name or date of birth that doesn't match your certificates exactly.
  • Forgetting to download and save the final submitted form and payment receipt.

How do I find a Sarkari Job that matches my qualification?

Use the qualification filters on this page to sarkari job find openings suited to 10th pass, 12th pass, diploma, graduate, or postgraduate candidates, sorted by sector and state.

सरकारी फॉर्म ऑनलाइन 2026 में आवेदन कैसे करें?

सबसे पहले संबंधित विभाग की आधिकारिक अधिसूचना पढ़ें, पात्रता जांचें, फिर वैध ईमेल और मोबाइल नंबर से रजिस्ट्रेशन करके फॉर्म भरें, दस्तावेज़ अपलोड करें और आवेदन शुल्क जमा करें।

Is OnlyJobs reliable for sarkarijob updates?

Yes - OnlyJobs has tracked sarkarijob notifications since 2011, cross-verifying every listing against official department websites before publishing.

What is the difference between a Sarkari Job and a private-sector job?

Sarkari jobs offer government-backed job security, pension (NPS/OPS), fixed working hours, and statutory benefits, while private jobs typically offer market-driven pay with fewer long-term security guarantees.

Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 – FAQ's

How to apply for Anganwadi Recruitment 2026 online?

Visit your state's official WCD / ICDS portal (link provided in table above). Register with mobile & Aadhaar, fill the application form, upload documents (photo, 10th certificate, Aadhaar, domicile), and submit before the last date. Print the application acknowledgement slip after submission.

What is the eligibility for Anganwadi Worker 2026?

Candidates must have passed 10th or 12th standard from a recognized board. Age limit is 18–35 years (varies by state). Must be a permanent resident of the ward/village for which vacancy exists. Only female candidates are eligible for Worker and Helper posts.

What is the salary of Anganwadi Worker in 2026?

Anganwadi Worker receives a monthly honorarium of ₹10,000–₹20,000 depending on the state (Karnataka and TN are highest at ~₹14,000). Anganwadi Helper gets ₹5,000–₹7,000/month. The Central Government pays ₹4,500/month as base honorarium, and states add their own component on top.

Is there a written exam for Anganwadi jobs?

No, there is no written examination for Anganwadi Worker and Anganwadi Helper posts. Selection is purely merit-based on academic qualification marks (10th / 12th percentage). For Supervisor / CDPO posts, a written exam or interview may be conducted depending on the state.

What is the age limit for Anganwadi Helper?

Age limit is 18 to 35 years as of 1st January 2026 in most states. SC/ST candidates get 5 years relaxation (maximum age 40). OBC candidates get 3 years relaxation (maximum age 38). PwD candidates get additional relaxation as per state rules.

What documents are required for Anganwadi job application?

Required documents: Aadhaar card, 10th/12th marksheet and certificate, domicile/residence certificate, caste certificate (SC/ST/OBC), passport-size photograph, scanned signature, and EWS/PwD certificate if applicable. Graduation certificate is needed for Supervisor post applications.

What is ICDS recruitment 2026?

ICDS stands for Integrated Child Development Services - the government programme under which Anganwadi centres operate nationwide. ICDS recruitment 2026 refers to hiring of Anganwadi Workers, Helpers, Supervisors, and CDPOs by state WCD departments under the Ministry of Women & Child Development (wcd.nic.in).

Is Anganwadi Worker a permanent government job?

Anganwadi Workers and Helpers are honorary workers, not regular government employees. They receive a fixed monthly honorarium (not salary) and are entitled to benefits like ESI, health insurance, and maternity benefits. Supervisors and CDPOs are regular government employees in most states and receive full pay & grade pay.

Can I apply for Anganwadi job from a different district?

No. Anganwadi Workers and Helpers must be permanent residents of the same ward/village/district where the vacancy exists. A domicile or residence certificate is mandatory. Applications from outside the specified locality are rejected. For Supervisor/CDPO posts, the same district residency rule generally applies.

Forest Department Posts List

The forest department offers a range of posts across different levels, from ground-level field roles to gazetted officer positions. Most current openings on this page are for Group C posts - Forest Guard, Forester, Beat Guard, and Field Guard - making this a common landing point for anyone searching forest department group c recruitment 2026.

  • Forest Guard - entry-level field post responsible for forest protection and anti-poaching patrols
  • Forester - supervises Forest Guards and manages a forest beat or range sub-unit
  • Forest Beat Officer - field-level post combining patrol, record-keeping, and community liaison duties; commonly searched as forest beat officer notification 2026
  • Range Forest Officer (RFO) - manages an entire forest range, includes administrative and enforcement responsibilities
  • Assistant Conservator of Forests (ACF) - gazetted officer post, typically recruited through state forest service exams
  • Indian Forest Service (IFS) Officer - recruited through UPSC, the highest field-level forestry cadre in India

Eligibility for Forest Department Jobs 2026

Educational Qualification

  • Forest Guard / Forest Watcher / Field Guard: 10th or 12th pass from a recognized board
  • Forester: 12th pass, often with Science subjects; some states require a diploma in Forestry
  • Range Forest Officer: Graduate degree, frequently in Science, Agriculture, or Forestry
  • ACF / IFS: Graduate degree in a relevant discipline (Botany, Zoology, Forestry, Agriculture, Veterinary Science, Engineering, or Environmental Science), followed by the respective state or UPSC exam

Age Limit & Relaxation

The general age limit for Forest Guard and Forester posts is usually 18–27 years, though this varies by state. Age relaxation is generally available for SC/ST (5 years), OBC (3 years), PwBD candidates, and other reserved categories as per government norms.

Reservation & Age Relaxation for Ex-Servicemen

Most state forest departments reserve a fixed percentage of Forest Guard, Forester, and Beat Guard posts for ex-servicemen, in addition to SC, ST, OBC, and EWS reservations. Candidates applying for jobs for ex servicemen in forest department typically receive:

  • Additional age relaxation, usually 3–5 years beyond the general age cap (or as per length of military service)
  • Relaxed physical standards in several states
  • A reserved vacancy quota, separate from the general merit list

Exact quota percentages and relaxation norms differ by state, so always cross-check the specific notification before applying.

Physical Standards

Most Forest Guard and Forester posts require candidates to clear height, chest measurement (for male candidates), and a Physical Efficiency Test involving running, walking, or trekking - since the job involves regular field patrol duty in forest terrain.

Selection Process & Exam Pattern for Forest Officer & Forest Guard Posts

The selection process for forest department recruitment generally involves multiple stages, designed to test both academic knowledge and physical fitness given the field nature of the job.

Written Exam, PET/PST & Document Verification

  1. Written Examination - objective-type questions on General Knowledge, General Science, Reasoning, Mathematics, and sometimes Forestry/Environment-related topics
  2. Physical Efficiency Test (PET) / Physical Standard Test (PST) - running, walking/trekking distance, height and chest measurement
  3. Document Verification - verification of educational certificates, age proof, category certificates, and (where applicable) ex-servicemen discharge documents
  4. Medical Examination - fitness check before final appointment
  5. Final Merit List - based on combined written exam and PET/PST scores, as per each state's weightage formula

Syllabus Highlights for Forest Guard & Ranger

  • General Knowledge & Current Affairs
  • General Science (Physics, Chemistry, Biology basics)
  • Basic Mathematics / Numerical Ability
  • Reasoning & Mental Ability
  • State-specific General Knowledge (local geography, forests, wildlife sanctuaries)
  • For Ranger/RFO level: Forestry science, environmental laws, and wildlife protection acts

Note: Apprenticeship posts (under the Apprentices Act) are not regular government jobs but are a popular no-exam entry route into PSUs and railways for ITI/diploma/graduate candidates, offering valuable hands-on experience.

Two Types of No Exam Govt Jobs

No-exam recruitment in India falls into two patterns, and knowing which one a notification belongs to tells you exactly what to prepare for:

Type Typical Posts Who it's for How Selection Works
Fresher - no exam, usually no interview Apprentice, GDS, trainee 10th/12th/ITI/Diploma/Graduate pass Merit list prepared from academic marks
Experienced - no exam, interview-based Officer, manager, specialist, medical Professionals with relevant work experience Shortlisting based on qualification/experience, followed by a personal interview

How Recruitment Without Exam Works in Government Jobs

This section explains the different routes through which government departments fill vacancies without conducting a written competitive exam.

1. Direct Recruitment

Certain senior and specialised posts - such as Chairman, Member, and Secretary in Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) and State Public Service Commissions (PSCs) - are filled through direct recruitment based on eligibility criteria like qualifications, experience, and domain expertise, rather than a written exam. Similarly, some administrative posts in the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) may be filled through direct recruitment.

2. Sports Quota Recruitment

Government organisations such as Indian Railways, the Indian Army, and Public Sector Banks reserve a quota of posts for candidates with outstanding achievements in sports at the state, national, or international level. Eligible candidates can be appointed to posts like Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, and Clerk without going through the regular written exam.

3. Cultural Quota Recruitment

Indian Railways also recruits individuals with exceptional talent in arts, fine arts, music, or literature under the cultural quota for posts such as Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, and Assistant Loco Pilot.

4. Internal Promotions and Deputation

Government departments, including the Indian Administrative Service (IAS) and Indian Police Service (IPS), promote existing employees to higher posts based on performance, seniority, and experience - without requiring them to clear a fresh competitive exam. Ex-servicemen and defence personnel are also often considered for civilian government posts through deputation or reservation quotas, without a written exam.

5. Apprenticeships and Trainee Programmes

Railways, PSUs, and central organisations like DRDO and BEL regularly hire Act Apprentices, Trade Apprentices, and Project Trainees through merit lists based on academic marks - with no written entrance test.

6. Walk-in Interviews

Some government and PSU organisations directly call candidates for walk-in interviews based on their qualifications and experience, especially for technical, medical, and contractual roles.

Government Jobs Without Exam by Sector

This section breaks down no-exam opportunities by sector - banking and railways - which are among the most common areas where such recruitment occurs.

Bank Jobs Without Exam

While most public sector bank recruitment (PO, Clerk, SO) happens through IBPS or bank-specific written exams, some banks fill specific posts - such as Local Bank Officer and certain Specialist Officer roles - through direct recruitment, where the bank shortlists applications based on eligibility criteria and conducts an interview instead of a written test.

Railway Jobs Without Exam

Indian Railways and the various Railway Recruitment Boards/Cells (RRBs/RRCs) offer no-exam entry through:

  • Act Apprentices (selection via academic merit list)
  • Sports Quota posts (Assistant Station Master, Ticket Collector, Clerk)
  • Cultural Quota posts (Junior Clerk, Ticket Collector, Assistant Loco Pilot)
  • Scouts and Guides Quota

Before You Apply: How to Spot Fake "No Exam" Job Offers

No-exam recruitment is the single biggest magnet for job fraud in India, because "direct joining, no exam" is exactly what scammers promise. Four rules protect you:

  1. No genuine government post is ever sold. Nobody - agent, "officer", consultancy - can arrange selection for money. The only payment in real recruitment is the application fee, paid on the official portal, typically a few hundred rupees.
  2. Verify the notification on the official domain. Every real notice lives on a .gov.in, .nic.in or official PSU domain. Every row in our list links to the post page where the official notification PDF and apply link are attached - if an offer you received isn't traceable to an official notice, treat it as fraud.
  3. No recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram DMs. Forwarded "joining letters" and interview calls demanding a deposit are scams, full stop.
  4. Cross-check suspicious notices against PIB Fact Check before sharing or paying anything.

How to Apply for Government Jobs Without Exam

  1. Open the post from the live list and read the official notification PDF - eligibility, age limits and fee are final there, not in any summary.
  2. Confirm you match the qualification and category requirements before paying any fee.
  3. Apply on the official portal linked in the notification; keep the registration number and fee receipt.
  4. For merit-list posts (GDS, apprentice), enter marks exactly as on your certificates - mismatches reject applications at verification.
  5. Track the post page for merit list / shortlist updates, or subscribe to WhatsApp/Telegram alerts so deadlines and results reach you automatically.

Government Jobs Without Exam - FAQs

1. Are there really government jobs without an exam?

Yes. Apprenticeship intakes, India Post GDS, sports and cultural quota posts, walk-in interviews and direct recruitment for experienced candidates are all filled without a written competitive exam. The live list at the top of this page shows every such notification currently open.

2. Which government jobs have no exam and no interview at all?

India Post GDS and Railway/PSU Act Apprentice selections use only a merit list of academic marks - there is no written test and no interview. Everything depends on your Class 10 (and ITI/diploma, where applicable) percentage.

3. What no-exam options exist for freshers after 10th, 12th or ITI?

Apprenticeships, GDS and trainee posts are the main fresher routes. Selection is a merit list prepared from academic marks, which is why these notifications attract very high application volumes despite no exam.

4. Can experienced professionals get a government job without an exam?

Yes. PSUs and autonomous bodies fill officer, manager and specialist posts by shortlisting candidates on qualification and experience, followed by a personal interview - no written test.

5. Are government jobs without exam permanent?

Often not. Apprenticeships are roughly one-year training engagements with a stipend, and many walk-in posts are contractual with fixed tenure. Direct-recruitment posts can be regular - the notification states the nature of each post, so check before applying.

6. Are there bank jobs without an exam?

A few. Some banks fill specialist and local officer posts through shortlisting plus interview. Bank apprenticeship drives vary - some are merit-based while others include an online test - so read each notification's selection clause.

7. Are there railway jobs without an exam?

Yes: Act Apprentice intakes (merit list), sports quota, cultural quota and Scouts & Guides quota. Apprentice intakes are large; the quota routes are small zonal recruitments with their own assessment process.

8. Is India Post GDS really without an exam?

Yes - selection is an online merit list generated from Class 10 marks, with no exam and no interview. Because of that, GDS is heavily targeted by paid-selection scams; apply only through the official GDS portal.

9. How do I identify fake "no exam" job offers?

No genuine government post is sold, fees are paid only on official portals, and no recruitment happens over WhatsApp or Telegram messages. Verify every offer against the official notification on a government or PSU domain - if it isn't there, it's fraud.

10. How often is this list updated?

Daily. New notifications are added as they release, and every listing is removed automatically after its last date, so the list only ever shows posts you can still apply for.

Govt Jobs for Law Graduates - Eligibility (LLB, LLM, BL)

Eligibility varies by post, but the core requirement for almost every government law job is a recognised law degree. Senior and specialised roles add experience, an LLM, or Bar enrolment on top.

Educational Qualification

  • Bachelor of Law (BL) / LLB (Legum Baccalaureus): the baseline qualification for most legal and law officer posts.
  • LLM (Master of Laws): required for senior legal officer, faculty, and some advisory positions.
  • Integrated 5-year degrees - BA LLB, BBA LLB, BCom LLB - are accepted wherever an LLB is required.

The degree must be from a university recognised by the Bar Council of India.

Bar Council Enrolment & AIBE

For litigation, prosecutor, and standing-counsel roles you generally need to be enrolled as an advocate with a State Bar Council, and many positions ask for the All India Bar Examination (AIBE) Certificate of Practice issued by the Bar Council of India. Purely advisory or research posts (Law Clerk, Research Fellow, Legal Consultant) often do not require enrolment.

Age Limit & Relaxations

The upper age limit is typically 30 to 40 years for the general category, depending on the post and recruiter. Statutory relaxations apply: usually 3 years for OBC, 5 years for SC/ST, and additional relaxation for PwD and ex-servicemen candidates. Always confirm the exact limit and cut-off date in the official notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

Salary & Pay Scale for Government Law Jobs

Pay depends on the organisation and grade. Officer-level legal posts under the 7th Pay Commission generally fall in Pay Levels 10 to 12, with a monthly salary roughly between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500, plus Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance, and other benefits. PSU legal officers are paid on IDA scales, which can be higher at entry grade.

Types of Law Officer / Legal Posts in Government Sector

  • Judicial Services - Civil Judge (Junior Division), Additional District Judge, High Court Judge, recruited via State Judicial Service Exams (PCS-J)
  • Law Officer / Legal Officer - Roles in public sector banks (IBPS SO Law), insurance companies (LIC AAO Legal), regulatory bodies (SEBI Grade A Legal), and PSUs (Coal India, NTPC, GAIL Legal)
  • Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor - Administrative legal support roles in ministries, universities, and district courts
  • Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO) - Prosecution roles recruited through State PSCs, requiring LLB and often a minimum years of practice

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, ADJ, High Court Judge)

Judicial Services is the most prestigious and highest-paying career path for LLB graduates. Recruitment happens through State Public Service Commissions (e.g., RPSC, UPPSC, MPPSC) via a three-stage exam: Preliminary, Mains, and Interview. Civil Judge posts typically require 0-3 years of practice depending on the state, while some states allow fresh LLB graduates to apply directly.

Law Officer / Legal Officer (Banks, PSU, Insurance)

Public sector banks and insurance companies recruit Law Officers through specialist officer (SO) exams. These posts require only an LLB degree (AIBE not mandatory) and offer competitive pay scales under the 7th Pay Commission equivalent structure, along with allowances.

Legal Assistant & Legal Advisor Posts

These are typically Group B/C administrative-legal posts in ministries, universities, and PSU legal departments, requiring an LLB degree and sometimes relevant drafting/litigation experience.

Assistant Public Prosecutor (APO)

APO recruitment is conducted by State PSCs (e.g., RPSC Assistant Prosecution Officer) and requires an LLB degree, enrollment as an advocate, and in most states, a minimum period of practice (often 3 years).

Selection Process for Law Govt Jobs

The selection process differs by post but commonly includes:

  1. Written examination - testing legal knowledge, aptitude, and general awareness (for judicial services and most exam-based posts).
  2. Interview / viva-voce - assessing legal reasoning and suitability.
  3. Document verification - degree, Bar enrolment, AIBE, age, and category certificates.

Advisory and consultant posts are often filled by shortlisting and interview alone, without a written exam.

Law Govt Jobs FAQ's

What are the latest law govt jobs in 2026?

Current law government jobs in 2026 include Law Officer, Legal Officer, Assistant Prosecution Officer, Judicial Service, and Legal Adviser posts across High Courts, PSUs, public sector banks, and central/state departments. The table above is updated daily with vacancy count, last date, and the official notification link.

Which departments hire LLB and law graduates?

High Courts and District Courts, the Ministry of Law and Justice, UPSC, State Public Service Commissions, public sector banks, PSUs, insurance companies, and regulatory bodies regularly recruit law graduates for legal and judicial roles.

What is the eligibility for government law jobs?

Most posts require a Bachelor of Law (LLB/BL) from a recognised university; senior roles may require LLM and experience. Litigation and prosecutor posts usually require enrolment with a State Bar Council and, often, the AIBE certificate.

What is the salary of a Law Officer in the government sector?

A government Law Officer or Legal Officer typically earns between ₹56,100 and ₹1,77,500 per month under the 7th Pay Commission, depending on the organisation, plus DA, HRA, and allowances. PSU legal officers draw IDA-scale pay.

Can a fresher LLB graduate get a government job?

Yes. Freshers can apply for Civil Judge (Junior Division) judicial-service exams, Law Clerk and Research Fellow posts in High Courts, and trainee legal roles. Some PSU and bank Law Officer posts require a few years of post-enrolment experience.

How can I apply for law officer vacancies in central government?

Open the post in the table above, read the official notification, register on the recruiter's portal, fill in the application with your LLB and enrolment details, pay the fee, and submit before the last date.

What is the difference between Judicial Services and Law Officer posts

Judicial Services (Civil Judge, via state judiciary exams) places you on the bench as a judge. Law Officer/Legal Officer posts are departmental legal-counsel roles in PSUs, banks, and ministries - advisory and litigation support, recruited by interview or written test.

Is there an age limit for govt law jobs?

Most posts set the upper age at 30 to 40 years for the general category, with statutory relaxations for OBC, SC/ST, and PwD candidates. Check each notification, as judicial-service and PSU limits differ.

Union Bank of India has released the Union Bank Recruitment Project 2026–27 (Officers with Domain Expertise, General Banking Officers & Specialist Officers) notification for a total of 395 vacancies spanning General Banking Officers and Specialist Officers, from Manager (MMGS-II) up to Deputy General Manager (TEGS-VI). Online registration opens on 21 July 2026 and closes on 15 August 2026. This article covers important dates, vacancy break-up, eligibility, age limit, salary, application fee, selection process, and the step-by-step application procedure, based strictly on the official notification issued by the Bank's Human Resources Vertical, Central Office, Mumbai, dated 20.07.2026.

Candidates should download and read the official notification PDF from the Bank's website before applying. Official website: www.unionbankofindia.co.in

Union Bank of India Recruitment 2026: Eligibility Criteria (Post-wise)

Nationality/Citizenship

An applicant must be: (i) a citizen of India, or (ii) a subject of Nepal, or (iii) a subject of Bhutan, or (iv) a Tibetan refugee who migrated to India before 1 January 1962 with the intention of permanently settling in India, or (v) a person of Indian origin who has migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire, Ethiopia, or Vietnam with the intention of permanently settling in India. Candidates under categories (ii)–(v) must hold a certificate of eligibility issued by the Government of India before the date of this notification.

Union Bank of India Recruitment 2026: Selection Process

For posts up to Scale III, selection may comprise Online Examination, Group Discussion (if required), and/or Personal Interview, depending on the number of applicants. For posts in Scale IV, V, and VI, selection may comprise Group Discussion (if required), any other test/assessment, and/or Personal Interview. The Bank reserves the right to add, cancel, or modify the selection method for any notified post.

Quantitative Aptitude, Reasoning, and English Language sections are qualifying in nature - marks in these are not counted toward final merit. All tests except English Language are available bilingually (English and Hindi). Minimum qualifying marks: 40% for General/EWS categories, 35% for reserved categories (SC/ST/OBC/PwBD), subject to the Bank's discretion. There is a penalty of 25% of the marks assigned to a question for each wrong answer; unattempted questions carry no penalty.

Personal Interview

A Personal Interview of 100 marks assesses academic and job knowledge, power of expression, clarity of thought, leadership qualities, communication skills, and suitability for the post. Minimum qualifying marks: 50 for General/EWS, 45 for Reserved Category (SC/ST/OBC/PwBD). Candidates are called for interview in the ratio of 1:3 against the number of vacancies (subject to change at the Bank's discretion).

Final Merit

Final selection is based on the aggregate marks of Online Examination and Personal Interview (or Personal Interview alone, or GD/other assessment plus Personal Interview, depending on which stages are conducted), prepared in descending order category-wise, up to the number of vacancies. In case of a tie, the candidate senior in age (earlier date of birth) is ranked higher.

Appointment letters, salary certificates, and pay slips are not accepted as proof of work experience.

Union Bank of India Recruitment 2026: How to Apply

  1. Visit the official website www.unionbankofindia.co.in and click on the 'Recruitment' page.
  2. On the Career Overview page, click 'Click to View the Current Recruitment' to open the link "UNION BANK RECRUITMENT PROJECT 2026-27 (OFFICERS WITH DOMAIN EXPERTISE, GENERAL BANKING OFFICERS & SPECIALIST OFFICERS)".
  3. Click on "CLICK HERE TO APPLY ONLINE" to open the online application form.
  4. Choose "Click here for New Registration" and enter your Name, contact details, and Email ID. Note down the system-generated Provisional Registration Number and Password.
  5. Use the "SAVE AND NEXT" option to fill the application in stages if needed, and verify all details carefully - no changes are allowed after clicking "COMPLETE REGISTRATION".
  6. Upload photograph, signature, and left thumb impression as per the prescribed specifications.
  7. Fill in the remaining application details, preview the form, and click "COMPLETE REGISTRATION".
  8. Click on the "Payment" tab and pay the applicable application fee online.
  9. Click 'Submit' and save/print the system-generated application form and e-receipt for future reference.

Candidates can apply for only one post. Only the last valid, complete application will be retained in case of multiple submissions. An application, once submitted, cannot be withdrawn, and the fee is non-refundable.

Union Bank of India Recruitment 2026: Important Instructions

  • Application can be made for only one post; multiple appearances for a single post at interview will lead to cancellation of candidature.

  • Existing Union Bank of India employees may apply through proper channel (HR Department of Regional/Zonal Office) and, if selected, must resign and rejoin the Bank's service afresh.

  • Selected candidates for posts S01–S108 must execute a Service Indemnity Bond to serve the Bank for a minimum of 3 years, or pay ₹2,50,000 plus applicable taxes if they leave before completing 3 years.
  • Selected candidates shall be posted at any Branch/Office of the Bank throughout India at the Bank's sole discretion.
  • The Bank reserves the right to change/modify the number of vacancies, examination structure, or cancel the recruitment process at any stage.

📄 Complete Details & Notification

Punjab National Bank (PNB) has invited online applications for recruitment to 545 posts of Local Bank Officer (LBO) in Junior Management Grade Scale-I (JMGS-I). The vacancies are distributed across 17 states, and candidates can apply for only one state based on their eligibility and language proficiency. Online registration is open from 20.07.2026 to 16.08.2026. This article covers all details of the notification, including state-wise vacancies, eligibility, salary, selection process, and how to apply.

  • Official Notification: Recruitment of Local Bank Officers in Punjab National Bank

Key Points on Vacancy Distribution

  • Candidates belonging to reserved categories for which no vacancy has been announced in a state may apply against Unreserved (UR) vacancies of that state, if they meet UR eligibility criteria.
  • Candidates can apply for a vacancy in one state only. Applying against one state makes a candidate ineligible to apply against any other state.
  • The merit list will be drawn state-wise and category-wise.
  • Selected candidates will be posted within the selected state until completion of nine (9) years of service or promotion to SMG Scale IV, whichever is earlier.
  • Prior experience will not be considered for seniority in service.
  • PwBD reservation is on a horizontal basis; selected PwBD candidates will be placed in their applicable category (SC/ST/OBC/EWS/UR) and posted within the state applied for, at locations identified suitable by the Bank.

PNB LBO Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Nationality/Citizenship

An applicant must be:

  • A citizen of India, or
  • A subject of Nepal, or
  • A subject of Bhutan, or
  • A Tibetan Refugee who came to India before 1st January 1962 with the intention of permanently settling in India, or
  • A person of Indian origin who has migrated from Pakistan, Burma, Sri Lanka, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Zambia, Malawi, Zaire, Ethiopia, or Vietnam with the intention of permanently settling in India.

Candidates in the last four categories must have a certificate of eligibility issued by the Government of India before the date of this notification, and must also be proficient in the local language of the state applied for.

Candidates who have completed their graduation in any discipline can also explore more Bank Officer Jobs and Graduate Government Jobs available across India.

Age and Educational Qualification

Post Scale Age (Years) Educational Qualification
Local Bank Officer (LBO) JMGS-I Min: 20, Max: 30 Graduate in any discipline from a University/Institution recognized/approved by the Government of India or its regulatory bodies

The candidate must possess a valid Mark-sheet/Degree Certificate confirming graduate status on the day of registration, and must indicate the percentage of marks obtained in Graduation while registering online.

Local Language Requirement

Candidates must be proficient in reading, writing, and speaking the specified local language of the state for which they are applying (as listed in the state-wise vacancy table). A Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT) will be conducted by an external agency for candidates who have not studied the local language as a subject in Class 10 or Class 12.

Post-Qualification Experience

  • Candidates must possess a minimum of one year of post-qualification work experience in Clerical/Officer Cadre in any Scheduled Commercial Bank or Regional Rural Bank listed in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934.
  • One advance increment is payable for each completed prior year of service as an Officer in Scheduled Commercial Banks (subject to a maximum of 2 increments), if the job profile matches that of a Scale-I Generalist Officer of PNB.
  • Candidates from subsidiaries of Scheduled Commercial Banks (Officer cadre) are eligible for only one advance increment under the same condition.
  • Proof of prior experience must be submitted in the prescribed format, duly certified by the previous employer.
  • Experience in other financial institutions will not be considered if the job profile does not substantially match that of a PNB Scale-I Generalist Officer.
  • No prior service/experience will be considered for seniority purposes.

Cut-off Dates for Eligibility

  • Age: Reckoned as on 01.07.2026
  • Mandatory Experience: Reckoned as on the closing date for online registration, i.e., 09.08.2026
  • Educational Qualification: Reckoned as on the closing date for online registration, i.e., 09.08.2026
  • The result of the qualifying examination must have been declared on or before 09.08.2026.
  • Candidates must indicate the percentage obtained in Graduation to the nearest two decimals; CGPA/OGPA must be converted to percentage as per the university's official conversion formula. A fraction of percentage will be ignored (e.g., 59.99% will be treated as less than 60%).

PNB LBO Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

Selection for the post of Local Bank Officer shall be conducted in four phases. The Bank reserves the right to decide whether all or any of these modes shall be adopted:

  1. Online Written Test
  2. Screening
  3. Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT), if applicable
  4. Personal Interview

Online Written Test Structure

Name of the Test No. of Questions Maximum Marks Sectional Duration (Minutes)
Reasoning & Computer Aptitude 25 25 35
Data Analysis & Interpretation 25 25 35
English Language 25 25 25
Quantitative Aptitude 25 25 35
General/Economy/Banking Awareness 50 50 50
  • There is negative marking: one-fourth of the marks assigned to each question is deducted for each wrong answer.
  • Minimum qualifying marks: 40% for General/EWS category, 35% for Reserved category, in each section. The Bank reserves the right to revise this at its discretion.

Screening

The online application and submitted documents of written-test-qualified candidates will be scrutinized to confirm eligibility before the Language Proficiency Test/Interview. Candidates found ineligible or with incorrect/false documents at any stage will be rejected from further participation.

Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT)

  • Candidates who have not studied the applied-for state's local language as a subject in Class 10 or 12 must appear for the LLPT.
  • The LLPT is qualifying in nature; candidates must secure the Bank-prescribed minimum qualifying marks to be considered for final selection.
  • Candidates who fail to qualify the LLPT are treated as ineligible for final selection, irrespective of performance in other stages.
  • Candidates who indicate they studied the local language in Class 10/12 are exempt from LLPT, subject to submission of valid documentary evidence at verification.

Personal Interview

  • All candidates shortlisted after qualifying the Online Written Test will be called for interview.
  • The Personal Interview carries 50 marks.
  • Minimum qualifying marks: 45% (22.50 marks) for SC/ST candidates; 50% (25 marks) for other candidates.
  • Candidates who fail to secure minimum qualifying marks in the interview will be disqualified.

Final Selection

  • Final selection is based on combined performance in the Online Written Test and Personal Interview, subject to qualifying the LLPT (where applicable).
  • Candidates who fail the LLPT are ineligible for final selection even if they qualify in the written test and interview.
  • The merit list is prepared state-wise and category-wise.
  • In case of a tie, the older candidate (by date of birth) is placed higher in the merit list.

  • Experience Certificate in the prescribed format, along with appointment letter, salary slips, relieving letter, etc.
  • Any other relevant documents in support of eligibility

How to Apply for PNB LBO Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official PNB website: https://pnb.bank.in/, under Recruitment/Career.
  2. Click "CLICK HERE FOR NEW REGISTRATION" and enter basic personal details to generate a Provisional Registration Number and Password (also sent via Email/SMS).
  3. Re-login using the Provisional Registration Number and Password to complete the application form.
  4. Upload scanned images of photograph, signature, left-hand thumb impression, and hand-written declaration as per prescribed specifications (see below).
  5. Use "SAVE AND NEXT" to verify details before clicking "COMPLETE REGISTRATION" - no changes are allowed after this step.
  6. Pay the applicable application fee through the online payment gateway (Debit Card, Credit Card, Net Banking, IMPS, Wallets, or UPI).
  7. On successful payment, an e-receipt will be generated.
  8. Take a printout of the submitted application form and e-receipt for personal record; do not send these to the Bank.

Applications are accepted online only, from 20.07.2026 to 16.08.2026, through https://pnb.bank.in/. No other mode of application will be accepted.

The signature and hand-written declaration must NOT be in capital letters. Candidates must also capture a live photograph via webcam or mobile phone during registration.

PNB LBO Recruitment 2026: Important Instructions

  • Candidates who have earlier worked in PNB or its merged/amalgamated entities and were discharged for reasons other than VRS/Resignation are not eligible to apply.
  • Candidates against whom there are adverse reports regarding character, antecedents, or moral turpitude are not eligible to apply.
  • There is no reservation for Ex-Servicemen in direct recruitment to Officer Cadre; however, age relaxation applies as per Government guidelines.
  • Selected candidates must execute an Indemnity Bond to serve the Bank for at least 3 years, or pay Rs. 2,00,000/- if they leave before completing 3 years of service.
  • Candidates must maintain a minimum CIBIL score of 680 or above at the time of joining. This is not a pre-condition to apply, and candidates with no bank account are not required to produce CIBIL status.
  • Selected candidates will be designated "Local Bank Officer" and will be on probation for 2 years from the date of joining.
  • After induction training, LBOs will be deployed within the Circles of the state for which they were selected, and will remain posted in that state until completion of 9 years of service or promotion to SMG Scale IV, whichever is earlier.
  • No Travelling Allowance is payable for the Online Test and LLPT. Unemployed SC/ST candidates called for interview will be paid actual to-and-fro 2nd Class Rail/Ordinary Bus fare.
  • Candidates must possess a valid Aadhaar card; the Bank may conduct Aadhaar verification at various stages.
  • Any dispute arising from this recruitment is subject to the sole jurisdiction of the Courts situated at NCT of Delhi.
  • The Bank reserves the right to cancel or modify the recruitment process at any stage without prior notice.

Indian Overseas Bank (IOB) has released the IOB Local Bank Officer (LBO) Recruitment 2026-27 notification (Advt. Selected candidates will be posted only within the state for which they apply, for the first 12 years of service or until promotion to SMGS-IV, whichever is earlier.

Nationality/Citizenship

IOB Local Bank Officer Selection Process 2026-27

Selection is made through an Online Examination, followed by a Language Proficiency Test (LPT) for candidates who have not studied the applied state's local language in Std. X or Std. XII, and a Personal Interview.

There is a penalty of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer, with no penalty for unattempted questions. There is no sectional cut-off, but the minimum qualifying aggregate is 30% for reserved category candidates and 35% for unreserved candidates.

Language Proficiency Test (LPT)

Candidates shortlisted for the Personal Interview who have not studied the applied state's local language in Std. X or Std. XII must qualify an LPT before the interview. Candidates who fail the LPT will not proceed further in the selection process.

Personal Interview

The Personal Interview carries 100 marks. The minimum qualifying marks are 45% for reserved category candidates and 50% for unreserved candidates.

Final Selection

The weightage of Online Examination and Personal Interview is in the ratio of 80:20. The minimum aggregate score (Online Exam + Interview) required is 30% for reserved categories and 35% for unreserved category candidates. The final merit list is prepared state-wise and category-wise.

Probation and Bond

Selected candidates will be on probation for 2 years of active service from the date of joining. They must execute a Financial Service Indemnity Bond of ₹2,00,000 for rendering a minimum of 3 years of service.

How to Apply for IOB Local Bank Officer Recruitment 2026-27

  1. Visit the official IOB website, www.iob.bank.in, and open the "Careers" page.
  2. Click on "Recruitment of Local Bank Officers – 2026-27" and select the post to apply.
  3. Click "Click here to Register Online" and complete first-time registration.
  4. Note the system-generated Registration Number and Password sent by email/SMS.
  5. Log in and upload photograph, signature, left thumb impression and handwritten declaration as per the specified format.
  6. Fill in all required details in the online application form carefully and accurately.
  7. Pay the applicable application fee/intimation charges online.
  8. Click "Complete Registration" and take a printout of the submitted application form and fee e-receipt for future reference.

Applications can be submitted only online from 08.08.2026 to 24.08.2026. No other mode of application is accepted, and applications once submitted cannot be withdrawn.

Important Instructions

  • Candidates can apply for only one state; a candidate applying for one state's vacancy is not eligible to apply for any other state.
  • Selected candidates will be posted within the applied state for the first 12 years of service or until promotion to SMGS-IV, whichever is earlier.
  • Application Fee/Intimation charges, once paid, are non-refundable and cannot be adjusted against any other recruitment process.
  • If multiple applications are submitted for the same state, only the last submitted application will be considered.

  • Request for change of examination centre, Personal Interview date, or centre will not be entertained.
  • Candidates working in Government/Quasi-Government/PSU roles must produce a No Objection Certificate at the time of Personal Interview.

IOB LBO Examination Centres

The online examination will be conducted at various centres across India, including Chennai, Madurai, Coimbatore, Tiruchirappalli in Tamil Nadu; Bengaluru, Hubli-Dharwad, Mysuru in Karnataka; Mumbai/Thane/Navi Mumbai, Pune, Nagpur in Maharashtra; and Ahmedabad/Gandhinagar, Surat, Rajkot in Gujarat, among other centres nationwide. The Bank reserves the right to add, delete, or reassign examination centres based on response and administrative feasibility.

SBI Junior Associate Exam Pattern 2026

The selection process has three stages: Preliminary Examination, Main Examination, and (where applicable) a Local Language Proficiency Test. Both online tests carry negative marking of 1/4th mark for every wrong answer.

Phase I: Preliminary Examination Pattern

The Prelims is an objective test of 100 marks and 1 hour total duration, split into three separately timed sections. There is no sectional cut-off, but the Bank shortlists candidates for Mains based on aggregate marks (approximately 10 times the number of vacancies per category, subject to availability).

S.No. Test Name Medium of Exam No. of Questions Max. Marks Duration
1 English Language English 30 30 20 minutes
2 Numerical Ability English/Hindi (as per state) 35 35 20 minutes
3 Reasoning Ability English/Hindi (as per state) 35 35 20 minutes
Total 100 100 1 Hour

Phase II: Main Examination Pattern

The Main Exam is an objective test of 200 marks over 2 hours 40 minutes, with four separately timed sections. Only the aggregate marks obtained in the Main Examination are used to prepare the final merit list Prelims marks are not added at this stage.

S.No. Test Name Medium of Exam No. of Questions Max. Marks Duration
1 General/Financial Awareness English/Hindi (as per state) 50 50 35 minutes

3 Quantitative Aptitude English/Hindi (as per state) 50 50 45 minutes
4 Reasoning Ability & Computer Aptitude English/Hindi (as per state) 50 60 45 minutes
Total 190 200 2 Hr. 40 min.

Candidates must score minimum qualifying marks on aggregate, as decided by the Bank; there are no individual sectional qualifying marks, and sectional marks are not maintained separately.

Phase III: Local Language Proficiency Test (LLPT)

Provisionally selected candidates who have not studied the specified local language of the applied state in Class 10 or 12 must appear for the LLPT after Main Exam qualification but before joining. Candidates who submit a 10th/12th mark sheet showing the local language as a subject are exempted from this test.

S.No. Test Pattern Section No. of Passages No. of Questions Max. Marks

1 Non-Verbal Test Subjective 3 15 15

Candidates who fail to qualify the LLPT will not be offered appointment.

SBI Junior Associate Syllabus 2026 (Section-wise Guide)

The notification does not release a detailed, topic-wise syllabus it only names the test sections shown above. Based on the officially named sections, the following are the broad areas typically covered under each section for this kind of clerical-cadre banking exam. Treat this as a general study guide, not an official syllabus document.

Prelims Sections

  • English Language: Reading comprehension, cloze test, para jumbles, error detection, fill in the blanks, vocabulary-based questions.
  • Numerical Ability: Simplification, number series, quadratic equations, data interpretation, arithmetic problems (percentage, profit & loss, average, ratio, time & work, simple/compound interest).
  • Reasoning Ability: Puzzles, seating arrangement, syllogism, inequality, coding-decoding, blood relations, direction sense, alphanumeric series.

Mains Sections

  • General/Financial Awareness: Current affairs, banking and financial awareness, static general knowledge.
  • General English: Comprehension, grammar, vocabulary, sentence correction, and para-based questions at a slightly higher difficulty than Prelims.
  • Quantitative Aptitude: Data interpretation, data sufficiency, arithmetic word problems, number series, simplification/approximation.
  • Reasoning Ability & Computer Aptitude: Advanced puzzles and seating arrangement, logical reasoning, plus basic computer knowledge (fundamentals, MS Office, internet, and banking-related computer terms).

  • Submit the form and save/print the system-generated application form for your records (this printout is not to be sent to SBI).

Important Instructions

  • A wait list of up to 50% of vacancies (state-category wise) will be maintained and released quarterly, valid for one year from the date of declaration of the final result.
  • SBI reserves the right to cancel the recruitment process entirely at any stage.
  • SBI has clarified it does not endorse any external coaching platform or consultancy claiming to guarantee selection; candidates should rely only on the official career portal.

BoB Professionals Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

The selection process for BoB Recruitment 2026 may comprise Application Scrutiny, an Online Test, a Psychometric Test, and/or a Group Discussion and Personal Interview, as decided by the Bank for each post.

  • Online Test (if conducted): Tentative structure includes Reasoning (25 questions/25 marks), English Language (25 questions/25 marks), Quantitative Aptitude (25 questions/25 marks), and Professional Knowledge (75 questions/150 marks), for a total of 150 questions/225 marks in 150 minutes. Reasoning, English Language, and Quantitative Aptitude sections are qualifying in nature; only Professional Knowledge marks count toward the final result. There is a penalty of 0.25 marks for each wrong answer.
  • Psychometric Test/Personal Interview (PI): Conducted to assess personality, communication, problem-solving ability, efficiency, and willingness to work in any part of the country. The minimum qualifying marks for PI are 60% for General & EWS category and 55% for other reserved categories.
  • Final Selection: Based on combined scores from the Online Test and/or PI, subject to vacancies available under the respective category.

BoB Professionals Recruitment 2026 Documents Required

Candidates must produce the following original documents, along with self-attested photocopies, at the time of interview or any subsequent stage of selection:

  • Printout of the valid Interview Call Letter
  • System-generated printout of the online application form
  • Proof of Date of Birth (birth certificate or SSLC/Std. X marksheet)
  • Photo identity proof (PAN Card/Passport/Driving Licence/Voter's Card/Bank Passbook with photo/Aadhaar card, etc.)
  • Individual semester/year-wise mark sheets and final degree/diploma certificate
  • Caste certificate (for SC/ST/OBC candidates, in the prescribed format)
  • OBC non-creamy layer certificate (valid as on the date of interview)
  • Disability certificate in the prescribed format (for PwBD candidates)
  • Service/Discharge Book and pension payment order (for Ex-servicemen candidates)
  • No Objection Certificate from current employer (for candidates serving in Government/Quasi-Government/PSU/Bank)
  • Documents supporting work experience (appointment letter, salary slips, relieving letter, etc.)
  • Any other relevant document in support of eligibility

How to Apply for BoB Professionals Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the official Bank of Baroda website at www.bankofbaroda.bank.in and go to the Career section → Current Opportunities.
  2. Register online using a valid personal email ID and mobile number, which must be kept active till completion of the recruitment process.
  3. Fill in the online application form carefully, upload a scanned photograph, signature, and supporting documents such as Date of Birth proof, qualification certificates, experience letters, and category certificates, as per the specifications given in the notification.
  4. Verify all details before submitting, since no changes are permitted after clicking the Submit button.
  5. Pay the applicable application fee online through Debit Card, Credit Card, Internet Banking, or UPI.
  6. On successful payment, download and retain a printout of the e-receipt and the completed application form for future reference.

BoB Professionals Recruitment 2026 Important Instructions

  • Only candidates willing to serve anywhere in India should apply, as selected candidates will be posted at the Bank's absolute discretion.
  • Selected candidates will be on probation for a period of 12 months.
  • Candidates selected for JMG/S-I posts must execute a service bond to serve for a minimum of 3 years or pay an amount equivalent to three months' gross salary (not exceeding Rs. 2 lakh) if they leave before completing three years.
  • Candidates selected for MMG/S-II, MMG/S-III, and SMG/S-IV posts must execute a similar service bond, with the payable amount not exceeding Rs. 3 lakh.
  • Change of category is not permitted at any stage after registration of the online application.
  • There is no reservation for Ex-servicemen in the Officers' Cadre.
  • The number of vacancies, including reserved vacancies, is provisional and may vary according to the Bank's actual requirement.
  • Not more than one application should be submitted by a candidate; in case of multiple applications, only the latest valid (completed) application will be retained.

The Gandevi People's Co-Operative Bank Limited - commonly referred to as Gandevi Bank, and identifiable by its official domain GPCB (gpcb.bank.in) - has released a notification, dated 10 August 2026, inviting applications from eligible candidates for the post of Clerk (referred to as "Jr. Clerk" at one point in the notification) in its Clerical cadre. The Bank is headquartered at Parsiwad, P.B. No. 10, Gandevi – 396360, District Navsari, Gujarat.

Gandevi Bank intends to fill 13 positions in the Clerical cadre at various locations in the Bank's area of operation, in a phased manner. Any eligible candidate who aspires to join the Bank as Clerk is required to register for an Online Written Examination; candidates who appear and are shortlisted in this examination will subsequently be called for a Personal Interview conducted by the Bank at Gandevi. Candidates must be domiciled in Gujarat State, aged between 21 and 28 years as on 10 August 2026, and hold a Bachelor's degree (with specific exclusions and inclusions detailed in the Eligibility section) with at least 55% marks. Applications can be submitted only online, and no other mode of application will be accepted.

Post Clerk (Clerical cadre)

Clerk 13

Gandevi Bank Clerk Recruitment 2026 Eligibility Criteria

Eligibility is assessed as on 10 August 2026. Candidates must be domiciled in Gujarat State and must produce relevant original documents (with a photocopy) in support of their identity and eligibility, as and when called for. No change in the category, age, educational qualification, or other details provided during online registration will be permitted at any stage after submission of the application.

Educational Qualification

The minimum qualification for recruitment to the Clerical cadre is a Bachelor's degree in any discipline from a recognised university with at least 55% marks. However:

  • Candidates holding a Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) degree are not eligible.
  • Candidates holding degrees in Engineering are also not eligible, except those holding a degree in Information Technology or Computer Science (BE/B.Tech or equivalent).
  • Candidates who have passed CA Intermediate or CMA Intermediate are also eligible.

All educational qualifications must be from a recognised University/Institution, with the result declared on or before 10 August 2026 (proper documentary proof of the result declaration date must be submitted at the time of interview). The date of passing the qualifying examination will be reckoned as the date of passing appearing on the mark sheet/provisional certificate. Candidates should also have knowledge of Gujarati, English, and Computers.

Note on a second discrepancy in the source notification: The Eligibility section states that the qualifying result must be declared on or before 10.08.2026, while a separate clause in the Interview Documents section (item e) refers to the result being declared on or before 01.08.2026. This inconsistency exists in the official notification and has been reproduced here without alteration; candidates should confirm the correct cut-off date with the Bank.

The notification does not mention any age relaxation for reserved categories (SC/ST/OBC/PwD/Ex-servicemen, etc.); this detail is not specified.

Gandevi Bank Clerk Recruitment 2026 Application Fee

Category Fee
All candidates Rs. 500/- + 18% GST = Rs. 590/- (non-refundable)

The notification does not mention any fee concession or exemption for SC/ST/OBC/PwD/Ex-servicemen or other categories; the fee of Rs. 590/- (inclusive of GST) applies to all candidates as per the notification. Payment can be made only through online mode – Debit Cards (RuPay/Visa/MasterCard/Maestro), Credit Cards, Internet Banking, IMPS, or Cash Cards/Mobile Wallets. Bank transaction charges for online payment must be borne by the candidate. The fee, once paid, will not be refunded under any circumstances, nor held in reserve for any other examination.

Gandevi Bank Clerk Recruitment 2026 Age Limit

Particulars Details
Minimum Age (as on 10.08.2026) 21 years
Maximum Age (as on 10.08.2026) 28 years
Date of Birth Range Not earlier than 10.08.1998 and not later than 10.08.2005 (both dates inclusive)

Candidates should ensure that they meet the prescribed age limit as on the specified cut-off date. You can use our Age Calculator to check your exact age and confirm your eligibility before applying.

Gandevi Bank Clerk Recruitment 2026 Selection Process

Selection consists of an Online Written Examination followed by a Personal Interview. A candidate must qualify in both the Online Examination and the Interview to be considered for the subsequent recruitment process.

Online Examination Pattern

S. No. Name of the Test No. of Questions Maximum Marks Duration
1 Reasoning 40 40 40 minutes
2 English Language 40 40 40 minutes
3 Computer Knowledge 40 40 30 minutes
4 General Awareness (with special reference to Banking Industry) 40 40 30 minutes
5 Numerical Ability 40 40 40 minutes
Total 200 200 180 minutes

All test papers will be available only in English. The Bank reserves the right to modify the structure of the examination, which will be intimated through its website. A penalty of 1/4th of the marks assigned to a question is applied for each wrong answer (negative marking). Test-wise and total scores are reported with decimal points up to two digits, and scores may be equated across sessions to adjust for minor differences in difficulty level.

Examination Centres

The examination will tentatively be conducted in online mode at Surat, Vapi, and Vadodara. No request for change of examination centre will be entertained. The Bank reserves the right to cancel any examination centre, add other centres, or allot a candidate to a centre other than the one opted for, at its discretion. Candidates will appear for the examination at their own risk and expense.

Interview

Candidates shortlisted in the online examination will be called for a Personal Interview, to be conducted at Gandevi only. The centre, venue address, date, and time of the interview will be communicated through the interview call letter, downloadable from the Bank's website. Any request for a change in date/centre of the interview will not be entertained, though the Bank reserves the right to change these at its discretion under unforeseen circumstances.

Documents Required for Gandevi Bank Clerk Recruitment 2026

Documents Required at the Time of Examination

  • Valid Call Letter for the respective date and session of the examination
  • Original photo-identity proof for verification
  • Photocopy of the photo-identity proof

Documents Required at the Time of Interview

  • Printout of the valid Interview Call Letter
  • System-generated printout of the online application form registered for the examination
  • Proof of Date of Birth (Birth Certificate or SSLC/Std. X Certificate with DOB)
  • Photo Identity proof
  • Mark sheets and certificates for Graduation or equivalent qualification
  • No Objection Certificate (NOC), for candidates serving in Government/quasi-Government offices/Public Sector Undertakings (including Nationalised Banks and Financial Institutions)
  • Experience certificates, if any
  • Valid Domicile Certificate

Valid Photo Identity Proofs

PAN Card, Passport, Permanent Driving Licence, Voter's Card, Bank Passbook with photograph, Photo identity proof issued by a Gazetted Officer on official letterhead, Photo identity proof issued by a People's Representative on official letterhead, valid recent Identity Card issued by a recognised College/University, Aadhaar Card/E-Aadhaar Card with a photograph, Employee ID, or Bar Council Identity Card with photograph. Ration Card and Learner's Driving Licence are not valid ID proofs for this recruitment. The candidate's name on the call letter must exactly match the name on the photo identity proof; candidates who have changed their name (e.g., after marriage) must produce a Gazette notification, marriage certificate, or affidavit as proof.

How to Apply for Gandevi Bank Clerk Recruitment 2026

Applications must be submitted online only, through the Bank's official website www.gpcb.bank.in. No other mode of application will be accepted.

Before You Begin: Documents to Keep Ready

  • Scanned photograph (200 x 230 pixels preferred, 20–50 KB, recent colour passport-size, light background)
  • Scanned signature in black ink, not in capital letters (140 x 60 pixels preferred, 10–20 KB)
  • Scanned left thumb impression on white paper in black or blue ink (240 x 240 pixels at 200 DPI, i.e. 3 cm x 3 cm; 20–50 KB; JPG/JPEG format)
  • Scanned hand-written declaration in English, not in capital letters, in the candidate's own handwriting (800 x 400 pixels at 200 DPI, i.e. 10 cm x 5 cm; 50–100 KB; JPG/JPEG format). The declaration text is: "I ___________ (Name of the candidate), hereby declare that all the information submitted by me in the application form is correct, true and valid. I will present the supporting documents as and when required."
  • A valid personal email ID and mobile number, to be kept active until the recruitment process is completed

Steps to Apply Online

  1. Visit www.gpcb.bank.in and click on "APPLY ONLINE".
  2. Choose "Click here for New Registration" and enter your Name, Contact details, and Email ID. A Provisional Registration Number and Password will be generated and also sent by email/SMS – note these down.
  3. Use the "SAVE AND NEXT" option to fill the form in stages if needed, and verify all details carefully, as no change will be possible after clicking "Complete Registration".
  4. Upload your photograph and signature as per the specifications above.
  5. Fill in the remaining details of the application form.
  6. Use the Preview tab to check the entire form before final submission.
  7. Click "Complete Registration" only after verifying that the photograph, signature, and all other details are correct.
  8. Click "Payment" and complete the online fee payment.
  9. Click "Submit" to complete your application.
  10. Take a printout of the system-generated online application form and the e-Receipt for the fee payment, for your records.

All particulars submitted in the online application will be treated as final; no change or modification is allowed after submission. Not more than one application should be submitted by any candidate; in case of multiple applications, only the latest valid (completed) application will be retained, and the fee paid for other registrations will be forfeited.

Important Instructions

  • Merely applying, appearing, and being shortlisted in the examination and/or interview does not imply that a candidate will necessarily be offered employment; the Bank is not liable to assign any reason for rejecting a candidate.
  • A candidate's admission to the examination, shortlisting for interview, and subsequent processes are strictly provisional. If it is found at any stage that a candidate does not fulfil the eligibility norms or has furnished incorrect/false information, the candidature will be rejected; if detected after appointment, services are liable to be summarily terminated.
  • Candidates should not carry mobile phones, pagers, calculators, or similar communication/electronic devices into the examination premises; the Bank cannot assure safekeeping of such items, and any infringement will lead to cancellation of candidature and possible debarment from future examinations.
  • Use of unfair means, impersonation, misbehaviour in the exam/interview hall, or disclosure/transmission of test content can lead to disqualification, debarment from future Bank examinations, criminal prosecution, or termination of service if already appointed.
  • Online applications, once registered, cannot be withdrawn, and the application fee once paid will not be refunded or held in reserve for any other examination.
  • Appointment of selected candidates is subject to being declared medically fit and to the Bank's service and conduct rules.
  • No hard copy of the call letter or Information Handout will be sent by post or courier; candidates must download these from the Bank's website using their Registration Number and Password/Date of Birth.
  • Canvassing in any form will lead to disqualification of the candidate.
  • Any dispute arising out of this advertisement or the recruitment process is subject to the sole jurisdiction of the Courts situated at Gandevi.
  • In case of any dispute arising from interpretation of a version of this advertisement other than English, the English version available on the Bank's website will prevail.
  • All further announcements and details relating to this recruitment process will be published only on the Bank's authorised website, www.gpcb.bank.in.

This notification is purely for apprenticeship training and does not guarantee employment.

Other Eligibility Conditions

  • Applicants must be resident and/or registered with a local Employment Exchange within Tamil Nadu, with registration date not beyond the application's last date, except wards of Railway employees.
  • Wards of Railway employees must submit the Railway employee's Identity Card/Service Certificate (attested by a Gazetted Officer), along with UMID card and PPO copy as proof.
  • Vacancies for Persons with Benchmark Disabilities are reserved trade-wise, subject to permissible disability categories and a minimum of 40% relevant disability; a disability certificate from the Central/State Government is required to claim this benefit.

ICF Act Apprentice Age Limit

Age will be reckoned as on 7 September 2026.

  • ITI candidates: must have completed 15 years and not completed 24 years of age.
  • Non-ITI candidates: must have completed 15 years and not completed 22 years of age.
  • Upper age relaxation: 5 years for SC/ST candidates, 3 years for OBC candidates.
  • Upper age relaxation for Persons with Disability: 10 years.
  • SC/ST candidates must produce a caste certificate, and OBC candidates must produce an OBC Non-Creamy Layer certificate, at the time of Document Verification.

Candidates are advised to check whether they satisfy the prescribed age limit before applying. Use our online Age Calculator to calculate your exact age instantly.

ICF Act Apprentice Application Fee

  • A processing fee of ₹100 plus applicable service charges (non-refundable) must be paid online.
  • No application fee is required for SC, ST, PwBD, and Women candidates.
  • No request for refund of fee once remitted will be entertained under any circumstances.
  • After successful payment (for candidates other than SC/ST/PwBD/Women), a unique Transaction ID starting with "DU" is sent to the registered mobile number and should be preserved for future reference.

ICF Act Apprentice Selection Process

  • The merit list is prepared based on marks obtained in Std X. For COVID-pass candidates in Std X, proof of the IX std mark sheet or X std half-yearly mark sheet duly signed by the Principal will be considered.
  • If two candidates have equal marks, the candidate with older age is preferred; if dates of birth are also the same, the candidate who passed Std X earlier is considered first.
  • Freshers exercise trade options, and trades are allotted based on merit order and vacancy availability; once allotted, requests for change of trade are not entertained. Candidates selected against benchmark disabilities are allotted only the trade permissible to them.
  • Ex-ITI candidates are trained in the trade for which they hold an ITI certificate.
  • Selected candidates must be physically fit as per the Apprentices Act, 1961 and Apprentices Rules, and must produce a Medical Certificate from a Government-authorised doctor (not below the rank of Assistant Surgeon) at Document Verification.
  • Selected candidates must execute a contract of apprenticeship; if a candidate is a minor, their guardian executes the contract as per the guidelines of the Regional Director of Apprenticeship Training, Guindy, Chennai.
  • Original Transfer Certificate for the qualifying examination (Std X/XII/ITI) must be produced during document verification.

How to Apply for ICF Act Apprentice Recruitment 2026

  1. Visit the ICF web portal at pb.icf.gov.in.
  2. Read the notification thoroughly before filling the online application form.
  3. Keep all relevant documents/certificates and a recent passport-size photograph (maximum 200 KB, jpg/jpeg format) ready before starting the form.
  4. Fill in the required details and submit the application; a system-generated registration number will be issued as the individual Registration ID, with the date of birth (in ddmmyyyy format) as the password for the acknowledgement.
  5. Pay the processing fee of ₹100 plus applicable service charges online (not applicable for SC/ST/PwBD/Women candidates).
  6. Check all details carefully before clicking the submit button.
  7. Generate and print the system acknowledgement after final submission; this printout is required at the time of Document Verification.

Candidates are not required to send any documents or the application form to ICF through Post, e-mail, FAX, or by hand. All communication from ICF will be sent only by SMS (from "PBICF") or email to the mobile number and e-mail ID mentioned in the application, so candidates should maintain the same contact details until selection is complete.

Also Read: RRB JE 04/2026 Recruitment 2026 Notification Out - Apply Online for 4098 Junior Engineer Posts

ICF Act Apprentice Important Instructions

  • This notification is purely for apprenticeship training and not for employment; no employment is guaranteed to apprentices on completion of training.
  • Imparting training at ICF confers no right to absorption in Railways after successful completion, as per the Apprenticeship Rules, 1991.
  • Canvassing in any form will disqualify the candidature, and no correspondence will be entertained in this regard.
  • If any declaration furnished by a candidate is found false, they will be disqualified or terminated at any stage of training without notice.
  • Accommodation must be arranged at the candidate's own cost; ICF will not provide food or accommodation.
  • Candidates selected for training will not be allowed to withdraw except for reasons beyond their control; those who wilfully remain absent are liable to refund the full training cost and stipend paid.
  • For clarifications, candidates may use the helpdesk at pb.icf.gov.in/act2026_cc/helpdesk_entry.php.

East Coast Railway (ECoR), through its Railway Recruitment Cell (RRC) Bhubaneswar, has released the ECoR GDCE Recruitment 2026 notification (No. ECoR/Pers/RRC-GDCE/2026, dated 07.08.2026) for the General Departmental Competitive Examination (GDCE). This exam fills up 25% of the net Direct Recruitment Quota vacancies in Safety and Non-Safety category posts, spread across 1421 posts including Assistant Loco Pilot, Station Master, Goods Trains Manager, Junior Engineer, Technicians, Junior Clerk cum Typist, and Commercial Clerk cum Ticket Collector.

Important: ECoR GDCE 2026 is not an open-market recruitment. Only regular and eligible employees of East Coast Railway (including the erstwhile Waltair division/SCoR), excluding RPF/RPSF staff, who currently hold lien in ECoR, can apply. ECoR GDCE Eligibility Criteria

It only states the applicable 7th CPC Pay Level for each post: Assistant Loco Pilot and Technicians - Pay Level 2; Commercial Clerk cum Ticket Collector - Pay Level 3; Goods Trains Manager - Pay Level 5; Station Master and Junior Engineer - Pay Level 6. Exact monthly salary/pay matrix figures are not specified in the notification.

ECoR GDCE Selection Process

Selection under ECoR GDCE 2026 follows a single-stage Computer Based Test (CBT), followed by post-specific additional stages, Document Verification, and Medical Examination:

Post Exam Mode Additional Test
Assistant Loco Pilot CBT (120 min, 100 questions) Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)
Station Master CBT (90 min, 120 questions) Computer Based Aptitude Test (CBAT)
Goods Trains Manager CBT (90 min, 120 questions) None
Junior Engineer CBT (120 min, 150 questions) None
Technicians CBT (90 min, 100 questions) None
Junior Clerk cum Typist CBT (90 min, 120 questions) Computer Based Typing Skill Test (CBTST)
Commercial Clerk cum Ticket Collector CBT (90 min, 120 questions) None
  • There is negative marking in CBT: 1/3rd mark deducted for each wrong answer. There is no negative marking in CBAT.
  • Minimum qualifying marks in CBT: UR – 40%, OBC (Non-Creamy Layer) – 30%, SC – 30%, ST – 25% (relaxable by 2 marks for PwBD candidates in case of shortage against reserved vacancies).
  • Shortlisting for CBAT/Typing Skill Test is done at 8 times the number of vacancies, based on CBT merit.
  • For ALP, final merit uses 50% weightage for CBT and 50% for CBAT. For Station Master, it is 70% CBT and 30% CBAT.
  • Candidates equal to the number of vacancies are called for Document Verification, based on CBT/CBAT merit.
  • Final appointment is subject to passing the prescribed Medical Fitness Test.

How to Apply for ECoR GDCE Recruitment 2026

Eligible ECoR employees must apply online through the official RRC Bhubaneswar website. A single online application is required even when applying for multiple posts.

ECoR GDCE Apply Online

  1. Visit the official website www.rrcbbs.org.in and click on the ECoR GDCE 2026 application link.
  2. Fill in personal details and bio-data carefully in the online application form.
  3. Upload a recent colour passport-size photograph (35mm x 45mm, JPEG format, up to 100 KB) and a scanned signature (JPEG, 10–40 KB).
  4. Keep scanned self-attested copies of date of birth, educational/technical qualification, caste certificate, and PwBD certificate (as applicable) ready before applying.
  5. Review all entered details carefully, then click the register button - once registered, no changes can be made to the application.
  6. Note the unique application number generated after registration and download/print the filled application in PDF format.
  7. Get the printed application forwarded by the controlling officer and upload the signed, scanned copy under the supporting documents tab (mandatory).

RRB Group D Application Status 2026: The Railway Recruitment Boards (RRBs) have issued a revised notice on the application status for CEN No. 09/2025 (Level-1) recruitment. Candidates can now check their updated application status provisionally accepted, conditionally accepted, or rejected by logging in at www.rrbapply.gov.in. RRB Group D Application Status 2026 - Overview

Particulars Details
Recruitment RRB Group D (Level-1 posts)
CEN Number CEN No. 09/2025
Conducting Body Railway Recruitment Boards (RRB), Ministry of Railways
Notice Type Revised Notice on Application Status

Revised Status Available From August 9, 2026, 9:00 PM
Status Check Website www.rrbapply.gov.in
Status Categories Provisionally Accepted, Conditionally Accepted (with conditions), Rejected (with reasons)
Notification Date August 9, 2026

RRB Group D Application Status: Categories Explained

Candidates can now view their updated status under three categories:

  • Provisionally Accepted: The application has been accepted on a provisional basis. It is not a final confirmation, and RRB can still cancel the candidature at any later stage if any discrepancy is found.
  • Conditionally Accepted: The application has been accepted subject to certain conditions. Candidates must check the specific conditions mentioned against their application and follow RRB's instructions.
  • Rejected: The application has been rejected, and the reason for rejection will be shown along with the status.

Also Read: RRB Group D Admit Card 2026

How to Check RRB Group D Application Status 2026

  1. Visit the official RRB application portal: www.rrbapply.gov.in.
  2. Log in using your registered user credentials.
  3. Navigate to the application status section for CEN No. 09/2025.
  4. View your status: Provisionally Accepted, Conditionally Accepted, or Rejected.
  5. If rejected, check the reason for rejection displayed against your application.
  6. Save or take a screenshot of the status page for future reference.

Important Instructions for Candidates

  • The list of provisionally eligible candidates has been prepared carefully, but RRB reserves the right to rectify any inadvertent error or typographical/printing mistake.
  • RRB will not entertain any correspondence from ineligible or rejected candidates.
  • Candidature of all eligible/accepted candidates is purely provisional and can be cancelled at any stage of the recruitment process or even afterward if any inconsistency, deficiency, falsified record, or malpractice is found.
  • Candidates should refer only to official RRB websites for recruitment updates and must not rely on unauthenticated sources.
  • RRB has warned candidates to stay alert against touts who make false promises of selection in exchange for illegal consideration. The RRB recruitment process is fully computerized, and selection is based purely on merit.

Also Read: RRB Group D City Intimation Slip 2026

What to Do After Checking Your Status

If your application shows as provisionally or conditionally accepted, continue preparing for the next stage of the CEN 09/2025 recruitment process as and when RRB announces it. If your application is rejected, review the stated reason; RRB has clarified that it will not respond to correspondence from rejected candidates on this matter.
